```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Root locator + dual-load idiom shared with the get-started vignette:
# the source tree (check and site-build contexts) loads through pkgload; a
# bare installed package (reader-side) loads through library().
.pkg_root <- function() {
  for (dd in c(".", "..", "../..")) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "DESCRIPTION")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(dd, "R", "treatment-report.R"))) return(normalizePath(dd))
  }
  NA_character_
}
PKG <- .pkg_root()
if (!is.na(PKG) && requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
  suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(pkgload::load_all(PKG, quiet = TRUE,
                                                      export_all = TRUE)))
} else {
  library(msuiter)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

De-novo extraction (`ms_extract()`) discovers signatures; reference fitting answers
the mirror-image question. Given a trusted signature dictionary, `ms_fit()` estimates
each sample's exposure to every dictionary signature, `ms_test_presence()` asks which
signatures the cohort's evidence supports at all, and `ms_fit_bootstrap()` attaches
bootstrap confidence intervals and support stability to the same fit. This guide walks
the three faces on one small simulated cohort, then reads the `MsFit` result object and
the bootstrap plotting faces. The upstream steps (variants, tallying) are covered in
[get-started.html](get-started.html).

## A simulated cohort against COSMIC signatures

The dictionary is a channels x signatures matrix, or an `MsSignature` whose
`signatures` matrix is used. The bundled COSMIC reference database ships canonical
SBS96 matrices whose rows already carry the canonical channel labels, so slicing a few
columns gives a dictionary that `ms_fit()` can align by label.

```{r dictionary}
refdb <- ms_refdb_bundled(build = "GRCh38")
sbs <- refdb[["SBS_GRCh38"]]@matrices[[1]]
dict <- sbs[, c("SBS1", "SBS5", "SBS13", "SBS4")]
dim(dict)
```

A subgroup of samples plants an APOBEC signature on top of the clock-like pair; another
dictionary signature is planted nowhere, so the presence test below has something to reject.

```{r simulate}
samples <- paste0("T", 1:12)
act <- matrix(0, nrow = ncol(dict), ncol = length(samples),
              dimnames = list(colnames(dict), samples))
act["SBS1", ] <- 0.45
act["SBS5", ] <- 0.45
act["SBS13", samples[1:4]] <- 0.10
# share exposures: rebalance the clock pair so every column sums to one
resid <- 1 - colSums(act)
act["SBS1", ] <- act["SBS1", ] + resid / 2
act["SBS5", ] <- act["SBS5", ] + resid / 2
cat <- ms_simulate(dict, act, arm = "multinomial", burden = 600, seed = 11)
cat
```

`ms_simulate()` returns an `MsCatalog`, exactly the input `ms_fit()` dispatches on.

## Fitting exposures with ms_fit()

The default method, `"nnls"`, solves the Lawson-Hanson non-negative least squares
problem per sample: the classical deconstructSigs-style baseline. The other two
methods start from that solution and refine it on a likelihood scale:

- `"likelihood_bidirectional"` (MuSiCal flavour) alternates backward and forward
  steps on the per-mutation multinomial log-likelihood: a signature leaves when the
  cheapest removal costs less than the epsilon threshold and enters when the best
  gain exceeds it, until both steps decline;
- `"lrt"` (mSigAct flavour) maximizes the negative-binomial likelihood over the
  exposures through an internal safeguarded-Newton ascent, warm-started from NNLS.

```{r fit-nnls}
fit <- ms_fit(cat, dict) # method = "nnls" (default)
fit
head(fit@support)
head(fit@tests)
```

Two tidy evidence tables ride along. `support` holds one row per signature-sample
pair with the exposure, its compositional share and the zeroing decision:
exposures whose share falls below `zero_threshold` are set to exactly zero and
reported `active = FALSE`. `tests` holds the entry-wise presence LRT statistic and
raw p-value per pair, plus a Fisher standard error that exists only on the interior
support -- boundary parameters get tests, not intervals, so boundary rows carry `NA`.

Two further arguments shape the whole fit. `rescale = TRUE` (default) multiplies each
sample's kept exposures back onto the sample's original mutation total, the MuSiCal
TMB-rescale semantics: the multiplication leaves zeroed entries at zero, and the
shares (hence the zeroing decision) and the presence evidence are invariant.
`connected = NULL` by default; passing distinct dictionary column indices selects a
connected-signature group -- for example the clock-like background pair -- which is
fixed at its initial full-NNLS solution after the method refit (`FixAndRefit`) while
the remaining signatures are re-optimized against the residual. This is a documented
approximation of the upstream joint-refit strategy, which is declared future work and
never silently substituted.

## Choosing among the methods

All three methods run through the same kernel, and the `tests` evidence is
method-independent by construction: the LRT columns are always computed at the
negative-binomial MLE exposures, so the tables compare fairly across methods. The
`nb_size` argument is the negative-binomial size of every likelihood-based column;
larger values sit closer to the Poisson limit.

```{r fit-methods}
fits <- list(
  nnls = fit,
  bidirectional = ms_fit(cat, dict, method = "likelihood_bidirectional"),
  lrt = ms_fit(cat, dict, method = "lrt")
)
round(vapply(fits, function(f) f@exposures[, "T1"], numeric(ncol(dict))), 1)
```

## Testing cohort presence with ms_test_presence()

`ms_test_presence()` tests, per signature, whether the signature is present in the
cohort. Per-sample entry-wise LRT statistics are pooled by summation (independent
likelihoods add), and the raw p-value is the exact pooled-null tail: under the null
each per-sample statistic follows the Self-Liang boundary law (an equal mixture of a
point mass at zero and a chi-square), so the pooled statistic over independent
samples is a Binomial-weighted mixture of chi-squares. Benjamini-Hochberg correction
runs over the signature family, and `pass_bh` applies the frozen family-wise alpha.

```{r presence}
ms_test_presence(cat, dict) # kernel face: catalog + dictionary
ms_test_presence(fit)       # MsFit face: re-aggregates the fit's own evidence
```

The result is a plain data.frame with one row per dictionary signature, so it drops
into any downstream filter or report. The two faces agree by construction -- the
`MsFit` face re-derives its p-values from the fit's stored evidence grid with the
pure-R twin of the kernel's arithmetic.

## Bootstrap intervals and stability with ms_fit_bootstrap()

The bootstrap resamples each sample's mutations from its empirical channel
distribution (nonparametric multinomial), refits the selected method per replicate,
and reports the percentile interval over the replicate exposures plus the support
stability -- the frequency with which the zeroing rule keeps each exposure active.
The result is an `MsFit` like `ms_fit()` returns, enriched with attributes on the
exposures matrix; the `support` table gains a `boot_stability` column. The point
exposures and tests remain an ordinary point fit: the interval is support-conditional
evidence alongside the LRT, not a replacement for it. With `return_draws = TRUE` the
raw per-replicate exposure cube is attached as the `boot_draws` attribute for the
histogram face below; `bca = TRUE` adds the bias-corrected-and-accelerated interval
computed from the same replicates. The default replicate count is higher; this guide
keeps `n_boot` small for rendering speed.

```{r bootstrap}
boot <- ms_fit_bootstrap(cat, dict, method = "nnls", n_boot = 50, seed = 1,
                         return_draws = TRUE)
boot
head(boot@support)
names(attributes(boot@exposures))
dim(attr(boot@exposures, "boot_draws"))
```

The CI endpoints are labelled matrices with the same shape as the exposures, so the
interval for one sample reads directly as a table.

```{r boot-ci-table}
round(cbind(lower = attr(boot@exposures, "ci_lower")[, "T1"],
            estimate = boot@exposures[, "T1"],
            upper = attr(boot@exposures, "ci_upper")[, "T1"],
            stability = attr(boot@exposures, "support_stability")[, "T1"]), 1)
```

## The MsFit object and the bootstrap plots

The `MsFit` container carries the labelled `exposures` matrix (signatures x
samples), the `support` and `tests` data.frames, an adhoc `reference_summary`
snapshot derived from the dictionary's signature labels (a sha256 digest over the
labels, never an embedded reference database), and the `engine` string recording the
method. `print` shows one line with dimensions, engine and snapshot version; the
plotting faces read the bootstrap attributes directly.

```{r plot-ci, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
plot_boot_ci(boot, sample = "T1")
```

```{r plot-distribution, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
plot_boot_distribution(boot, sample = "T1") # requires return_draws = TRUE
```

```{r plot-stability, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
plot_boot_stability(boot, sample = "T1")
```

`plot_boot_ci()` draws the point exposures with their percentile whiskers for one
sample, ordered by exposure share; `plot_boot_distribution()` shows the raw
per-replicate exposure histograms with the estimate and both bounds marked;
`plot_boot_stability()` bars the support stability against the calibration floor.
Without the draws cube the histogram face raises a structured error that says to
re-run `ms_fit_bootstrap()` with `return_draws = TRUE`.

## Where to go next

Once signatures are fitted and their presence established, the natural next steps
are comparing dictionaries and extracted catalogs -- [Comparing
signatures](comparing-signatures.html) -- and the calibration statistics behind the
presence and interval machinery -- [Calibrated
statistics](calibrated-statistics.html). The input path from VCFs to catalogs is in
[get-started.html](get-started.html).
